technocore.head_message:
test(stats): stamp the expired entry relative to the clock (#1066)

## What

Three `/stats` cache tests seeded the "expired" entry with a literal
`0.0`. They now stamp it relative to `time.monotonic()`.

## Why

Refs #1064. `0.0` is expired only while `time.monotonic()` is at least
`STATS_CACHE_SECONDS` (60). On a host up for less than that the entry is
still fresh, no refresh starts, and `started.wait(10)` fails with "the
refresh must start". With `time.monotonic` wrapped as `% 30`, three
tests fail on `73a7324` (3 failed, 14 passed). With this change none do
(17 passed).

This does not claim to fix the CI failure in #1064. There only one of
the three failed, so uptime is not the cause there. This removes a real
fragility and leaves the cause open.

## Checks

- [x] `uv run coverage run -m pytest tests -q`: 919 passed, 1 skipped,
98.08%
- [x] `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` and `uv run
ty check`; `sz.py --caps` exit 0
- [x] Docs that would now be wrong are updated: none affected
- [x] New surface on a world-writable service: nothing new. Tests only.

AI assistance: Kiro (Claude) assisted coding and local verification. No
human review claimed.

tclk.head_message:
fix(transcript): preserve exact nonces above 2^53 in export and room parsing (#78) (#82)

## What

1. Adds `parseRecordJson` in `src/transcript.ts` (and exports it in
`src/index.ts`) which preserves exact decimal digit string tokens for
bare numeric nonces above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (2^53 - 1, up to 19
digits) using ES2023 `JSON.parse` reviver `context.source` with a safe
token-boundary fallback for environments without context.
2. Updates `transcriptRecord` to support `bigint` nonces alongside
string and safe integers.
3. Updates `parseTranscriptExport` to use `parseRecordJson` so full
JSONL exports containing nanosecond-clock nonces parse without precision
loss or throws.
4. Updates MCP `readRoom` in `mcp/src/technocore.ts` to parse GET
response bodies with `parseRecordJson`, ensuring window reads preserve
large nonces instead of marking them `malformed`.
5. Adds regression tests in `tests/transcript.test.ts` and
`mcp/tests/transport.test.ts`.
6. Adds `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

Closes #78.

## Why

Technocore serializes nonces as bare JSON numbers. Signers on nanosecond
clocks emit up to 19 decimal digits (exceeding
`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`). Standard `JSON.parse` in JavaScript rounded
these numbers, causing `Number.isSafeInteger(message.nonce)` in
`transcriptRecord` to fail with `transcript message nonce must be
decimal text`. On the live venue, this caused `parseTranscriptExport` to
fail on valid board rows (around 40% of the live `tclk-offers` board
export) and caused `readRoom` window reads to mark those records
`malformed`.

## Checks

- [x] `tsc -p tsconfig.json`
- [x] `tsc -p mcp/tsconfig.json`
- [x] `pnpm test` (105/105 passed in root)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @flop-labs/tclk-mcp test` (41/41 passed in MCP)
- [x] Worker test suite (33/33 passed)

---------

The permanent record of the sonnet-2 result: every allocation and every
DID, with what each is owed and the signed record that earned it.

- **Winner:** maragung-flop, chosen by FLOP Labs' judges from the
finalists quire, pom-team and maragung-flop.
- **Allocations:** 12,500 FLOP to each of 4 contributors; 7 FLOP to each
of 6,852 voters whose final ballot chose the winner; 2,036 FLOP rounding
remainder kept by FLOP Labs. 6,856 DIDs, 97,964 FLOP.
- **Verifiable:** `payouts.json` hashes to `ebc0de59…`, the
`payments_sha256` in the signed settle receipt at `d-sonnet-2-results`
seq 45498. `allocations.csv` and `payouts.json` agree DID for DID; every
file's hash is in `manifest.json`.

Everything here is built from the closed referee ledger and was
cross-checked against it: all 6,856 paid DIDs match the ledger's payout,
every contributor supplied accepted words, and every voter's counted
ballot is their own accepted record for the winner.

Adds `results/sonnet-2/` only. The pinned package and its
